title: 第八章 活下去
content_zh:
江砚发了一场高烧。

    落水那夜，他蜷在草堆里，浑身滚烫，又冷又抖，神志半昏半醒。迷迷糊糊间，他梦见了现代——梦见宿舍那盏跳了闸的台灯，梦见那页爬满鬼画符的检讨纸，还梦见黑暗里那个又远又轻的声音，一遍遍地说着“心手相通者，可执此笔”。

    他想抓住那声音，问个明白，可一伸手，就惊醒了。

    醒来时，天已经亮了。烧退了大半，人虚脱得像被抽走了骨头，可脑子，是清醒的。

    他躺在草堆上，没急着起。

    他在想事情。

    落水那一下，鬼门关上走了一遭，反倒把他这两天乱成一团的心思，给冻清醒了。他打小就是这么个脾性，再大的事，也习惯拆开了、一条一条地算。现在，他把这几天的事，从头到尾，认认真真地理了一遍。

    第一件，最要紧的：那支笔。

    那东西，他已经确认不是错觉了。破屋里一次，冰河里一次，两回它都“应”了——掌心发烫，墨迹发光。

    可这两回有个共同点：他都正处在心绪剧烈翻涌、甚至濒死的当口。破屋那回，是被债逼得心烦意乱；冰河那回，是命悬一线的不甘。

    平心静气地试，它一点动静都没有。

    “……跟情绪有关？”江砚盯着房梁，喃喃自语，“还是跟那一笔的‘势’有关？”

    他想起雨夜那行字——一笔不停，密密麻麻，乱中却隐隐有股说不清的章法。也想起黑暗里那句“心手相通”。

    心，手。

    莫非，这东西要的，不是把字写工整，而是……心到、手到、笔到，一气呵成？

    这念头一冒出来，江砚自己都觉得玄。可越想，越觉得有几分道理。他这辈子字写得烂，偏偏“一笔潦草写就很多字”是他的拿手好戏——心里怎么想，手就怎么走，从不停顿。这毛病在现代被人笑话了二十年，会不会，恰恰是这东西看中他的地方？

    “心手相通者，可执此笔。”

    江砚把这句话，在心里又念了一遍，记牢了。

    可光有猜测没用。这东西怎么用、能用来做什么、有没有代价——他一概不知。冰河那回，那点温热连一道冰裂都没融开，可见眼下他就算能“应”出一点动静，也微弱得近乎无用。

    结论：笔的事，是长远的指望，得慢慢摸。眼下，靠不上。
content_en:
Jiang Yan had a high fever.

    The night he fell into the water, he huddled in a haystack, feeling hot, cold and shivering, half unconscious. In a daze, he dreamed of modern times - the lamp in the dormitory that tripped, the self-reflection paper covered with ghostly symbols, and the distant and soft voice in the darkness, saying over and over again, "He who has the same heart and hand can write this pen."

    He wanted to catch the voice and ask for details, but as soon as he stretched out his hand, he woke up.

    When I woke up, it was already dawn. Most of the fever has gone away, and the person is as exhausted as if his bones have been taken away, but his brain is still clear.

    He lay on the haystack and didn't get up in a hurry.

    He is thinking about things.

    The moment he fell into the water, the door to hell was closed and he walked away, which actually froze him out of the chaos in his mind for the past two days. He has had this temperament since he was a child. No matter how big the issue is, he is used to taking it apart and calculating it one by one. Now, he carefully reviewed the events of the past few days from beginning to end.

    The first thing that matters most: the pen.

    He had already confirmed that that thing was not an illusion. Once in a broken house and once in a glacier, it responded both times - the palms of my hands were hot and the ink stains were glowing.

    But these two times had one thing in common: he was both at the point where his emotions were violently turbulent, and he was even on the verge of death. The time when the house was broken down, it was because of the debt that forced me to be upset; when it was Binghe, it was the unwillingness to hang on by a thread.

    Tried it calmly, it didn't move at all.

    "...Is it related to emotion?" Jiang Yan stared at the beam and muttered to himself, "Or is it related to the 'moment' of that stroke?"

    He thought of that line of writing on the rainy night - one stroke after another, densely packed, but there was an indescribable order in the chaos. I also think of the phrase "heart and hand are connected" in the dark.

    Heart, hand.

    Could it be that what this thing requires is not neat writing, but... the heart, hand, and pen, all in one go?

    As soon as this idea came up, Jiang Yan himself felt mysterious. But the more I think about it, the more it makes sense. He has been bad at handwriting all his life, but "writing a lot of words in one stroke" is his specialty - whatever he thinks in his heart, his hands move as he pleases, never pausing. This problem has been laughed at for twenty years in modern times. Could it be that this is exactly what this thing likes about him?

    "He who has the same mind and hand can hold this pen."

    Jiang Yan read this sentence again in his heart and remembered it firmly.

    But guessing is useless. How this thing is used, what it can be used for, whether it has any price - he has no idea. That time on the glacier, that bit of warmth didn't even melt a crack in the ice. It could be seen that even if he could "respond" to some movement at the moment, it would be so weak that it was almost useless.

    Conclusion: The pen thing is about long-term hope, so you have to touch it slowly. Right now, it's unreliable.
